reason: The comparison row gives, in the Multi-AZ with two readable standbys column, up to 2x faster transaction commits compared to Multi-AZ with one standby.
The Available engines row lists the same six engines for Single-AZ and for Multi-AZ with one standby, and only PostgreSQL and MySQL for two readable standbys.

The failover row states Single-AZ needs a point-in-time restore that can take several hours with updates after the latest restorable time (typically last 5 minutes) unavailable, as quickly as 60 seconds for one standby, typically under 35 seconds depending on replica lag for two standbys.

The row states the 30-minute maintenance window for the first two options with Automatic Minor Version Upgrades, and typically under 1 second with an open source or RDS Proxy, typically under 35 seconds alone, for two readable standbys.
The row says None for Single-AZ and for one standby (only a passive failover target), and that the two standbys act as failover targets and serve read traffic.
The row states Multi-AZ deployments always span at least two Availability Zones within a single region, and read replicas can be within an Availability Zone, Cross-AZ, or Cross-Region.
The row gives main purposes: high availability, disaster recovery and local performance, scalability, in the three columns named in the claim.
The row states non-Aurora Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication and multi-Region deployments and read replicas use asynchronous replication.
The context shows the requires-downtime note under both Full load and Full load plus CDC, and the CDC option keeps the target available and migrates ongoing changes.
The quotes state console migration from EC2, on-prem or another cloud to RDS using AWS DMS with same engine and compatible versions; the context lists MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL.
The quote states DB snapshot copy charges apply to the data transfer and standard storage charges apply in the destination Region, on the backup replication page.
The note states automated backup replication isn't supported for Multi-AZ DB clusters but is supported for Multi-AZ DB instance deployments.

The quote states a DB instance can be restored to a specific point in time from a replicated backup; the page is about backups replicated to another Region and its engine notes only concern option groups.
The quote states that for disaster recovery a DB instance can replicate snapshots and transaction logs to a destination Region, copied as soon as they are ready.
The quote names Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL as sources for a read replica in a different Region; the scope keeps the availability caveat from the context.
The quotes state for MySQL and MariaDB that data transfer costs drop by creating one replica from the source and the others from that first replica.
The quote and its list state cross-Region replication incurs RDS data transfer charges for the initial snapshot and for each data modification sent out of the source Region.
The quotes state the replica uses the default security group and in most cases the default DB parameter group and option group; the Db2, MySQL and Oracle exceptions are kept in the condition.
The quotes state the source must be encrypted for an encrypted cross-Region replica and that you choose the KMS key in the destination Region.
The claim repeats the quote word for word.
The quote states a higher level of lag time for a replica in another Region, caused by longer network channels between regional data centers.
The quotes state promotion for Db2, MariaDB, SQL Server, MySQL and Oracle, and status terminated without promotion for PostgreSQL.
The three list items give disaster recovery, scaling reads to a Region closer to users, and easier migration between Regions.
The quotes state end of support on March 31, 2027 and no access to the RDS Custom for Oracle console or resources after that date.

The quotes state RDS Custom automates administration while giving access to the database environment and OS for legacy, custom and packaged apps, and that Amazon RDS doesn't let you access the underlying host.

The EC2 recommendation in the quote has two conditions (full management responsibility and simply need a managed compute service) and is about commercial databases; the claim drops the second condition and the word commercial.
The quote states Amazon RDS hosts the software components and infrastructure of DB instances and the customer is responsible for query tuning.
The mode table row for fleet-wide monitoring views says Not supported for Standard mode and Supported for Advanced mode.

The CLI step for --performance-insights-retention-period states the retention period must be at least 465 days to turn on Database Insights Advanced mode; the corpus shows the same rule in the modify section.
The FAQ quote states Database Insights inherits all Performance Insights capabilities plus fleet-level monitoring, APM integration and correlation with logs and events.
The quotes give up to 7 days at no additional cost in Standard mode, configurable 1 to 24 months beyond that with a pricing link, and 1-24 months at no additional cost in Advanced mode.
The quote states RDS enables the Standard mode of Database Insights by default for Amazon RDS databases.
The naming constraint list states 1-63 alphanumeric characters or hyphens, first character a letter, unique per account per Region; the hyphen rule is kept as a condition.
The Aurora row says use it when migrating or modernizing an on-premises relational workload or with less predictable query patterns, with MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible engines.
The quote suggests in-memory caching such as ElastiCache alongside the database, or a durable persistent in-memory database such as MemoryDB, for microsecond read response times.
The DynamoDB row gives key-value, session stores or shopping carts, and serverless NoSQL with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.
The RDS row names a fully managed relational database with six engines (listed) and optimization for structured data, full SQL, automated backups, patching and Multi-AZ.
The quote, in the context of installing the engine on EC2, states rehosting leaves upgrades, patches, backups, capacity planning, performance and availability targets to you.
The quoted cell states structured data stored in tables, rows and columns and that relational databases support complex queries through joins.
The quotes state re-platforming migrates the on-premises relational database to a fully managed RDS instance and makes no changes to the application.
